title: OSHA construction health hazards practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction health hazards practice questions on 29 CFR 1926 Subpart D: first aid, sanitation, noise, lasers, lighting, ventilation and lead.

questions.question: There is no infirmary, clinic, hospital or physician reasonably accessible in time and distance to the worksite. Who must be available at the worksite to render first aid?

options.A: A person with a valid first-aid training certificate from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or verifiable equivalent training
options.B: Any employee who volunteers, with no training needed
options.D: A licensed physician who stays on site full time

questions.explanation: In that case "a person who has a valid certificate in first-aid training from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or equivalent training that can be verified by documentary evidence, shall be available at the worksite to render first aid."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: In the absence of an infirmary, clinic, hospital, or physician, that is reasonably accessible in terms of time and distance to the worksite, which is available for the treatment of injured employees, a person who has a valid certificate in first-aid training from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or equivalent training that can be verified by documentary evidence, shall be available at the worksite to render first aid.

questions.question: How often must the employer check the contents of the first aid kit, under 1926.50(d)(2)?

options.A: Only when an employee reports that an item is missing
options.B: Before being sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job
options.C: Once a year, at the start of the construction season

questions.explanation: The kit contents "shall be checked by the employer before being sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job to ensure that the expended items are replaced."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The contents of the first aid kit shall be placed in a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item, and shall be checked by the employer before being sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job to ensure that the expended items are replaced.

questions.question: When must provisions be made for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury?

options.A: Within 24 hours after the first serious injury
options.B: When the project is half complete
options.C: Prior to commencement of the project
options.D: Only if the project lasts longer than 90 days

questions.explanation: "Provisions shall be made prior to commencement of the project for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Provisions shall be made prior to commencement of the project for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury.

questions.question: In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, what must be conspicuously posted?

options.C: The list of first aid kit contents
options.D: The telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances

questions.explanation: "In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, the telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances shall be conspicuously posted."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, the telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances shall be conspicuously posted.

questions.question: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, what must be provided within the work area?

options.A: Suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body, for immediate emergency use
options.B: A sign listing the nearest hospital
options.C: A first aid kit with extra bandages
options.D: A fan to blow vapors away

questions.explanation: "Suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.

questions.question: Under Table D-1 in 1926.51, what is the minimum number of toilet facilities for a jobsite with 20 or less employees?

options.A: None, if a portable water cooler is provided
options.C: 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 10 workers

questions.explanation: Table D-1 lists "20 or less" employees with a minimum of 1 facility; for 20 or more it lists "1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 40 workers."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: TABLE D-1 Number of employees Minimum number of facilities 20 or less 1. 20 or more 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 40 workers.

questions.question: What does 1926.51 say about the common drinking cup?

options.A: It is allowed if washed daily
options.B: It is allowed only on crews of fewer than 10
options.D: It must be marked with the crew name

questions.explanation: The rule says: "The common drinking cup is prohibited." Where single service cups are supplied, a sanitary container for unused cups and a receptacle for used cups must be provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The common drinking cup is prohibited.

questions.question: Where showers are required by a particular standard, how many showers must be provided?

options.C: One for each 25 employees of each sex
options.D: One for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift

questions.explanation: "One shower shall be provided for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: One shower shall be provided for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift.

questions.question: Under 1926.57(b), local exhaust systems must be designed so that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors or gases are handled in what way?

options.A: They are not drawn through the work area of employees
options.B: They are blown toward the nearest open window
options.C: They are drawn past the employees' breathing zone first
options.D: They are collected only at the end of each shift

questions.explanation: Local exhaust systems "shall be so designed that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors, or gases are not drawn through the work area of employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.57, Ventilation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Such exhaust systems shall be so designed that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors, or gases are not drawn through the work area of employees.

questions.question: Under Table D-2, Permissible Noise Exposures, what is the sound level (dBA slow response) for a duration of 8 hours per day?
questions.explanation: Table D-2 lists a duration of 8 hours per day at 90 dBA slow response; 95 dBA is listed for 4 hours and 100 dBA for 2 hours.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: TABLE D-2-PERMISSIBLE NOISE EXPOSURES Duration per day, hours Sound level dBA slow response 8 90 6 92 4 95 3 97 2 100

questions.question: When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding Table D-2, what must be utilized first?

options.D: Nothing, as long as a sign is posted

questions.explanation: "Feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized." If they fail to reduce sound levels within the table, PPE as required in subpart E "shall be provided and used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in Table D-2 of this section, feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized. If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal protective equipment as required in subpart E, shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table.

questions.question: Under 1926.52(e), exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed what level?
questions.explanation: "Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.

questions.question: Section 1926.59 (Hazard communication) says its requirements for construction work are identical to which section?
questions.explanation: The note in 1926.59 says the requirements applicable to construction work "are identical to those set forth at § 1910.1200 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.59, Hazard communication (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Note: The requirements applicable to construction work under this section are identical to those set forth at § 1910.1200 of this chapter.

questions.question: Under 1926.62(j)(1)(ii), the employer must institute a medical surveillance program for employees who are or may be exposed at or above the action level for more than how long?
questions.explanation: The program is required "for all employees who are or may be exposed by the employer at or above the action level for more than 30 days in any consecutive 12 months." Initial medical surveillance (blood lead and ZPP) is made available to employees exposed on any day at or above the action level.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall institute a medical surveillance program in accordance with paragraphs (j)(2) and (j)(3) of this section for all employees who are or may be exposed by the employer at or above the action level for more than 30 days in any consecutive 12 months;

questions.question: Employees in areas with a potential exposure to direct or reflected laser light greater than what level must be provided with antilaser eye protection?
questions.explanation: Employees in areas where "a potential exposure to direct or reflected laser light greater than 0.005 watts (5 milliwatts) exists, shall be provided with antilaser eye protection devices as specified in subpart E of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employees, when working in areas in which a potential exposure to direct or reflected laser light greater than 0.005 watts (5 milliwatts) exists, shall be provided with antilaser eye protection devices as specified in subpart E of this part.

questions.question: What must be done when a laser is left unattended for a substantial period of time, such as during lunch hour or overnight?
questions.explanation: "When the laser is left unattended for a substantial period of time, such as during lunch hour, overnight, or at change of shifts, the laser shall be turned off."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When the laser is left unattended for a substantial period of time, such as during lunch hour, overnight, or at change of shifts, the laser shall be turned off.

questions.question: Under 1926.55(b), equipment and technical measures used to keep exposure to air contaminants within the limits must first be approved for each particular use by whom?

options.A: A competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person

questions.explanation: "Any equipment and technical measures used for this purpose must first be approved for each particular use by a competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any equipment and technical measures used for this purpose must first be approved for each particular use by a competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person.

questions.question: Under Table D-3, what minimum illumination in foot-candles is listed for first aid stations, infirmaries, and offices?
questions.explanation: Table D-3 lists 30 foot-candles for "First aid stations, infirmaries, and offices." General construction plant and shops are listed at 10, and general construction area lighting at 5.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.56, Illumination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: 30 First aid stations, infirmaries, and offices.

questions.question: What is the permissible exposure limit (PEL) for lead in 1926.62(c)(1)?
questions.explanation: No employee may be exposed to lead "at concentrations greater than fifty micrograms per cubic meter of air (50 µg/m3) averaged over an 8-hour period." 30 µg/m3 is the action level.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall assure that no employee is exposed to lead at concentrations greater than fifty micrograms per cubic meter of air (50 µg/m3) averaged over an 8-hour period.

questions.question: How does 1926.62 define the action level for lead?

options.A: Any detectable lead in a blood sample
options.C: Any visible lead dust on a surface
options.D: Employee exposure, without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of 30 µg/m3 calculated as an 8-hour TWA

questions.explanation: Action level means employee exposure, "without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of lead of 30 micrograms per cubic meter of air (30 µg/m3) calculated as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Action level means employee exposure, without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of lead of 30 micrograms per cubic meter of air (30 µg/m3) calculated as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA).
